scope: three reserved technique searches, direct opens of returned sources, one reserved news search

sources.title: Match color between shots
sources.author: Adobe
sources.snapshot: Reference frame and side-by-side/split comparison are provided; face weighting can improve skin matching; automatic match can be replaced by choosing another reference.

sources.title: Color Correction Handbook, Chapter 9: Shot Matching and Scene Balancing
sources.author: Alexis Van Hurkman / O'Reilly
sources.date_note: Edition is identifiable by ISBN, but the opened page did not expose a reliable publication day.
sources.snapshot: Noticeable color or exposure differences can accentuate a cut and become continuity errors.

sources.title: darktable user manual: exposure
sources.author: darktable project
sources.date_note: Development manual page; current crawl verified, page publication date not stated.
sources.snapshot: Moving subject regions are unreliable brightness samples; equal numerical lightness can still look different when background ratios change.

sources.title: Exploring the combined impact of color and editing on emotional perception in authentic films
sources.author: Cao et al.
sources.snapshot: Behavioral and fMRI experiments found interactions between color and editing; authors state findings do not yet directly translate to practical parameters.

sources.title: AI-based relighting in moving images: current potentials, limitations, and implications for cinematographic practice
sources.author: Brenner, Schmid, Adamczyk
sources.read_scope: abstract, results, study limitations and metadata
sources.snapshot: Three workflows and expert interviews support selective correction, not replacement of on-set lighting; portrait texture/image integrity and temporal stability remain limitations.

sources.title: Claude Platform release notes
sources.author: Anthropic
sources.snapshot: Claude Models on Google Cloud launched with Google Cloud IAM and Marketplace billing; Opus 5.5 fast mode is available there.

notes: Search result references are conversation trace IDs, not permanent URLs. Exact tool-call clock was unavailable and was not invented.
